#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --nodes=1
#SBATCH --array=1-120
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --time=48:00:00
#SBATCH --mem=10GB
#SBATCH --job-name=ibs_dynamic
#SBATCH --mail-type=END
#SBATCH --mail-user=xl1005@nyu.edu
#SBATCH --output=ibs2_d3_p_%j.out

PROJECT_FOLDER="IBS-2-development"

model=psycho
#model=vstm
#model=fourinarow

proc_id=${SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID}

#var1='ibs_alloc'
#SPACE=' '
#var2='50'
#$method = "$var1${SPACE}$var2"
#method=ibs_3
#Nsamples=10
alpha=0.99
method=ibs_dynamic_3
#method=fixed
#method=fixed 
#method=fixedb
#method=exact


if [ $method = "exact" ]; then
    workdir=$SCRATCH/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/results/${model}/${method}/
else
    workdir=$SCRATCH/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/results/${model}/${method}${Nsamples}/${alpha}
fi

module purge. 
module load matlab/2020b
export MATLABPATH=$HOME/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/matlab
mkdir $SCRATCH/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/results
mkdir $SCRATCH/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/results/${model}
mkdir $workdir
cd $workdir

echo $model $method $Nsamples $proc_id

echo "addpath('$SCRATCH/${PROJECT_FOLDER}/matlab/'); recover_theta('${model}','${method}','${alpha}',${proc_id},${Nsamples}); exit;" 
cat<<EOF | matlab -nodisplay
%job_id = str2num(strjoin(regexp('$proc_id','\d','match'), ''))
job_id = str2num('$proc_id')
alpha = str2num('$alpha')
recover_theta('psycho','ibs_dynamic_3', alpha,job_id)

EOF

issues: The variable 'Nsamples' is used to construct the 'workdir' path but its definition '#Nsamples=10' is commented out. This will result in an incorrect directory path being created and used.
The 'mkdir' commands do not use the '-p' flag. The script will fail if any of the directories in the path already exist.

The final Matlab heredoc block uses hardcoded values ('psycho', 'ibs_dynamic_3') for the model and method arguments, ignoring the shell variables '$model' and '$method' defined earlier. This makes the variable assignments at the top of the script misleading and non-functional.
The command 'module purge.' contains a trailing period. The standard and more portable command is 'module purge'.
There is an 'echo' command that prints a Matlab command string to standard output, but this command is never executed. The actual executed Matlab code is different, which could be confusing.
